title: Non-deterministic throttling caused by late metadata merges in quota adjudicator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Observed intermittent throttles for a subset of keys after regional failover and route aliasing. Traffic that should have been allowed within burst credits was being denied for 100-400ms windows, manifesting as increased 429s and dropped requests. This ticket tracks investigation and fix for metadata merge timing in the quota adjudicator and credit reconciler which leads to non-deterministic enforcement.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two edge shards and route alias mapping for org 'acme' with per-key burst credits. 2) Start steady traffic from key A with intermittent spikes. 3) Trigger controlled failover of primary shard to replica (simulate network partition by blackholing shard sync). 4) Observe 429s in client logs for several hundred milliseconds after failover despite token availability in reconciled view.
reproduction_logs:
Grafana trace id: graf-9f3a2b. Sample logs: 2026-03-03T14:12:23Z [adjudicator] WARN key=A causal_metadata_merge_delay=120ms adjudicated=deny reason='stale-credits-after-merge'
2026-03-03T14:12:23Z [ingress] INFO request_id=... response=429 route=/v1/generate key=A shard=shard-7 reconcile_version=42 merge_version=41
root_cause: The adjudicator uses two asynchronous metadata streams: credit ledger updates and route metadata merges. On failover, the route alias/lookup metadata (which maps a request to a quota bucket) is applied after a fast-path credit snapshot is consumed, causing the adjudicator to evaluate quota against an outdated bucket. This race is exacerbated by our optimization that prefers earlier credit snapshots to avoid adding latency; when the metadata merge is late, enforcement can flip from allow to deny. Additionally, the per-org prefix cache lacked strong invariants during concurrent merges leading to occasional double-debit protection firing and transient denies.
impact: Users saw sporadic 429 spikes for a small percentage (~0.8%) of requests during shard failovers and route migrations. Billing accuracy is not materially affected long-term, but short denial windows materially degrade real-time experience for latency-sensitive customers. A few enterprise customers reported production incidents; customer_impact set to 'medium'.
proposed_fix:
1) Change adjudicator to wait for consistent metadata snapshot if merge timestamp > credit_snapshot.timestamp - add a bounded wait of 50ms. 2) Apply 'merge-first' ordering when route alias changes are detected during adjudication by checking merge_version; fallback to conservative allow with eventual reconciliation for non-critical endpoints. 3) Add per-key merge_version in fast-path to avoid consuming stale credits. 4) Add unit + integration tests simulating delayed metadata streams.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12891
rollforward_plan: Roll forward PR to canary cluster (canary-2) and run synthetic failover test harness for 48 hours. Monitor 429 rate on canary routes and compare to baseline. If stable, rollout to runtime-1.22 staging then gradual to prod with 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic steps.
rollback_plan: If canary shows increased 5xxs or >50% spike in 429s, revert PR and re-enable previous guardrails. Reconciliation job will run to clear any transient bookkeeping. Notify affected customers and open incident postmortem.
monitoring_changes:
- Add Grafana panel 'Adjudicator: late_metadata_merges' counting adjudicator denials with merge_delay>20ms.
- Add alert: if 429 baseline increases by 200% for a route during rollout, PagerDuty.
- Ship a synthetic probe that triggers shard failover every 6 hours to detect regressions.
